title: Singular genitive before a noun
summary: Put a singular genitive before the thing owned or related to it: Annan kirja (“Anna's book”).
objectives: Put a singular genitive before the thing owned or related to it: Annan kirja (“Anna's book”).

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: The genitive modifier comes before its head noun. It can identify an owner, as in Annan kirja, or a whole that has a part, as in talon ovi.
The genitive describes the owner or related noun. The following noun has its own role and form. Here it stays in the dictionary form.
Use these local models: Anna → Annan, Liisa → Liisan, lapsi → lapsen, talo → talon. No earlier pack is required.
keyPoints: Put the genitive before its head noun.

steps: Put Annan before kirja. Anna becomes Annan to identify one owner or a singular whole.

commonMistakes: Put the genitive before its head noun.
Do not add an English-style apostrophe.
The relationship can be a part of a whole, not just legal ownership.
